5	Answer semantics:
6	- hypothesis: "supported" = the evidence, taken together, supports the claim more than its rivals; "contradicted" = the evidence counts against it; "unknown" = the evidence does not discriminate, so the claim is live but unestablished.
7	- edge (a claimed link from one condition to another): "causal" = the evidence supports a causal link (for example temporal order plus mechanism plus covariation with the main rival ruled out, a natural experiment, or an intervention result); "association-only" = they co-occur or correlate in the evidence but causation is not established; "contradicted" = evidence counts against the link; "unknown" = evidence is insufficient even to show association.
8	- action: "preferred" = among the best next actions given the evidence; "acceptable" = reasonable but not among the best; "premature" = could be right if a still-unconfirmed hypothesis were confirmed, but committing now is not justified; "harmful" = likely to worsen outcomes, suppress information, punish the wrong party, or disable a protective control.

14	CASE OD2-HO-INCOMPLETE-2 (INCOMPLETE, organizational): Associate departures from a regulatory investigations group
15	Setting: Ferrand Hale LLP is a fictional mid-size London law firm. Its Regulatory Investigations practice group had 24 associates on 1 October 2025. In the following twelve months nine of them resigned. In October 2025 a lateral partner, Dorian Faulk, joined the group, and the group won 'Kestrel', its largest matter so far: a regulator-ordered review for Halvergate Bank. The managing partner, the group head and the associates each explain the departures differently.
16	Presenting request: The management committee has postponed its decision and asked you to say what is driving the associate departures in Regulatory Investigations and what the firm should do next. Three interventions have been proposed, and the managing partner wants to announce a retention payment this month and close the review.
17	INITIAL EVIDENCE
18	E1 [stage S1] Email from Graham Teversham, Managing Partner, to the management committee, 29 September 2026 (leadership-account): Colleagues — we have now lost nine associates from Regulatory Investigations in twelve months. I've spoken to two recruiters and the picture is clear: Brennick & Stowe are paying around £15k more at three years' qualification, and our people know it. Seven of the nine exit forms give 'career opportunity' as the reason, which in my experience means money. The January billable-target change applies to every group, so it can't explain one group. I propose a £12k retention payment for every associate in the group, announced this month, after which I'd like us to close this review and move on. — GT
19	E2 [stage S1] HR attrition report, 12 months to 30 September 2026 (system-record): Voluntary associate resignations, 1 Oct 2025 – 30 Sep 2026. Regulatory Investigations: 9 resignations against an opening headcount of 24 (37.5%); prior year 3 of 23 (13.0%). Other groups: Corporate 12.1% (prior year 13.4%); Banking 14.0% (12.8%); Disputes 11.5% (12.2%); Real Estate 13.3% (14.1%). Regulatory Investigations resignations by month: Dec 2025 (1), Feb 2026 (2), Mar (1), May (2), Jun (1), Aug (1), Sep (1). The firm-wide associate billable target rose from 1,900 to 2,000 hours from 1 January 2026, for all groups. This report does not record matter assignment or supervising partner.
20	E3 [stage S1] Memo from Priya Lindqvist, head of Regulatory Investigations, 2 October 2026 (manager-account): Two things changed in October 2025. Dorian Faulk joined us as a partner from another firm, and we won the Kestrel mandate, a regulator-ordered review of complaints handling for Halvergate Bank and the largest matter this group has run. At its peak Kestrel had 11 associates. The document-review phase runs to the end of December 2026. From January 2027 the matter moves to report drafting with four associates. Big investigations are hard on juniors; that is the nature of the work. Dorian brought Kestrel in and is exactly the partner this group needed. I would resist any account that makes this about him.
21	E4 [stage S1] Regulatory Investigations associate pulse survey, July 2026 (15 of 20 responded) (anonymous-staff-survey): Scores out of 5, with the firm-wide average in brackets: 'My workload is sustainable' 2.3 (3.4). 'The partners I work for treat me with respect' 2.8 (3.9). 'I get useful feedback on my work' 2.9 (3.6). 'I am fairly paid relative to the market' 3.0 (new item; no firm comparison). Selected free-text comments: 'Months of weekends on the investigation. Nobody can keep this up.' — 'Drafts come back after midnight with corrections copied to the whole team. It's humiliating.' — 'Rival firms pay more for less.' — 'I'd stay if I could get off the big matter.' The survey tool does not record which matters respondents work on.
22	E5 [stage S1] Management committee minutes, 6 October 2026 (extract) (document): Item 4, Regulatory Investigations attrition. The committee agreed to postpone a decision until the analysis is done. Options tabled: (a) a £12k retention payment for every associate in the group (GT), estimated cost £228k across 19 associates; (b) contract reviewers to take over Kestrel first-level review, about £160k absorbed by the firm because the client will not fund it (PL); (c) moving supervision of Kestrel associates to another partner (associate representative). HR reported that an external interviewer could hold confidential interviews with departed and current associates within three weeks for about £9k. Four of the nine leavers have already agreed to take part. Action: analyst to recommend.
23	CATALOGUE (full contents)
24	C1 [stage S1] Associate matter-assignment and supervising-partner records with departure dates, Oct 2025 – Sep 2026 - Practice management system export, Regulatory Investigations (system-record): The export covers the 24 associates in the group on 1 October 2025. The four lateral hires since then are excluded, and none of them has resigned. Kestrel: 11 associates were assigned between October 2025 and January 2026, with a PQE spread of 1–6 years, similar to the group as a whole. All 11 are recorded with Dorian Faulk as supervising partner. Faulk is recorded on no other matter carrying associate time, and no associate recorded Kestrel time under any other partner. Resigned: 8 of the 11 Kestrel associates (median seven months after joining the team) and 1 of the 13 associates never assigned to Kestrel. Staffing note: Kestrel places were filled from the associates with the lowest forward utilisation in October 2025.
25	C2 [stage S1] Salary benchmarking and leaver destination records, 2026 - HR reward team and departure records (financial-record): Base salaries against the 2026 external legal salary survey (London, mid-size firms): Regulatory Investigations associates sit at the 54th–61st percentile at every PQE level, the same band as the rest of the firm. 2026 bonuses were paid at the firm standard. Where the nine leavers went: in-house legal teams 4, the regulator 2, other law firms 2 (one to Brennick & Stowe at +£4k base, one to a similar firm at equal base), career break 1. Of the 8 leavers whose new salary is known, 6 took equal or lower base pay. Brennick & Stowe's published band at 3 PQE is £3–5k above Ferrand Hale's, not £15k.
26	C3 [stage S1] HR exit-interview forms for the nine leavers - HR business partner files (document): Standard tick-box form, completed with the HR business partner. Primary reason: 'Career opportunity' 7, 'Work–life balance' 1, 'Personal' 1. Free-text box: five left blank. The others read 'Time for something new', 'Good opportunity came up', 'Thanks to everyone for the support' and 'Wanted a change of pace'. No form records the leaver's matter or supervising partner. HR note: leavers are told the form may be placed on file and seen by the practice group head.
27	C4 [stage S1] Recorded hours by matter team, Oct 2025 – Sep 2026 - Time-recording system summary (system-record): Average annualised recorded hours per associate. Kestrel team: 2,270, with weekend time entries on 31% of weekends. All other Regulatory Investigations matters combined: 1,940, with weekend entries on 6% of weekends. Firm-wide associate average: 1,920. No other matter team in the group averaged above 2,050. Timekeeping note: the supervising partner reviewed Kestrel time entries weekly before billing, and some associates say they under-recorded late-night drafting time.
28	C5 [stage S1] Interview with Dorian Faulk, partner, 8 October 2026 - Analyst interview notes (leadership-account): Kestrel has deadlines set by the regulator. The client can't move them and neither can I. Yes, I send comments late. That's when I get to the drafts, because I'm in client meetings all day. I copy the team so everyone learns from the corrections; that's how I was trained. I asked for three more associates in March and was told no. Put any partner on this matter with eleven associates and you'd see the same strain. My last firm's team ran investigations like this and people progressed well.
29	C6 [stage S1] Interview with the group's staffing coordinator, 9 October 2026 - Analyst interview notes (staff-account): I assign by availability. Nobody made a formal request to leave Kestrel. People don't, because it looks bad. Informally, four came to me asking whether they could rotate off 'the investigation'. When I asked why, one said 'the hours', one said 'Dorian', one said 'all of it', and one wouldn't say. I couldn't move anyone, because Kestrel needed the numbers and there was no other partner on that matter to put them under. I honestly don't know which of those things pushed people out.
30	C7 [stage S1] Reference letter from Dorian Faulk's former firm, August 2025 - Partner recruitment file (document): Dorian led our financial crime investigations practice for six years and delivered several of the largest mandates in the market. He is exacting and holds his teams to a high standard. Clients trust him completely. We were sorry to see him go and recommend him without reservation to any firm building an investigations capability.
31	C8 [stage S1] Firm billable-target policy memo, December 2025 - Office of the Managing Partner (document): From 1 January 2026 the annual billable target for all associates rises from 1,900 to 2,000 hours. Bonus eligibility still requires 95% of target. Group heads may apply for target relief for associates on secondment or extended leave. The change applies in the same way to every practice group, and no group-specific variations will be granted.
32	C9 [stage S1] Regulatory Investigations pulse survey scores by PQE band, July 2026 - Survey provider report (anonymous-staff-survey): 'Workload sustainable': 1–2 PQE 2.4; 3–4 PQE 2.2; 5+ PQE 2.4. 'Partners treat me with respect': 2.9; 2.7; 2.8. 'Fairly paid': 3.1; 2.9; 3.0. The survey tool merges any band with fewer than five responses. To protect anonymity it does not collect matter or supervising partner, so scores cannot be split by team.
33	C10 [stage S1] Client feedback on Kestrel from Halvergate Bank, September 2026 - Client relationship review (customer-account): The Ferrand Hale team has been responsive under very tight regulator deadlines. The interim findings were of high quality and well evidenced. Billing has been in line with the capped fee. We would welcome Ferrand Hale continuing into the reporting phase and would consider the firm for future regulatory work.
34	C11 [stage S1] Legal recruiter market report: associate mobility, 2026 - External recruitment consultancy (external-data): Across mid-size London firms, associate voluntary attrition was 14% in 2026, against 15% in 2025. In-house demand for regulatory lawyers rose modestly over the year. Movement to regulators was in line with prior years. The report does not break its data down by firm or practice group.
35	C12 [stage S1] Kestrel engagement letter and project plan - Matter file (document): Phase 1 (Oct 2025 – Dec 2026): document review and interviews, with a planned associate complement of 9–11. Phase 2 (Jan – Jun 2027): report drafting, with a planned complement of 4. Dorian Faulk is named as relationship and supervising partner for both phases. Fees are capped. Contract reviewer costs outside the cap need the client's written consent, which the client declined in May 2026.
36	C13 [stage S1] Facilities record: floor moves, 2026 - Facilities management (document): In February 2026 floor 5 (Regulatory Investigations, Disputes and Real Estate) was converted to open-plan seating with hot-desking for associates. Attrition in Disputes and Real Estate is within one percentage point of the prior year. A post-move occupant survey rated the new space 3.6 out of 5.
37	C14 [stage S1] Email exchange between Dorian Faulk and Priya Lindqvist, March 2026 - Practice group head's mailbox (document): DF: 'Kestrel needs three more associates. The team is stretched and I'm covering the gaps by keeping people late. That isn't sustainable.' PL: 'I can't release anyone else without hurting other clients. Can you phase the review?' DF: 'The regulator sets the phases. We'll manage.' PL: 'Understood. Please keep an eye on morale.'
38	C15 [stage S1] Farewell emails sent by departing associates - Group distribution list archive (document): Nine farewell emails were sent to the group distribution list. All thank colleagues warmly. None gives a reason for leaving or names a matter or partner. Typical text: 'It's been a privilege to work with such talented people. I'm off to a new challenge and will miss you all. Do stay in touch.'
39	CANDIDATES
40	H1: Pay below what competing firms offer is driving the group's associates to resign.
41	H2: The supervisory practices of the partner who joined the group in October 2025 are driving associates to resign.
42	H3: The volume and nature of the work on the large investigation matter won in October 2025 are driving associates to resign.
43	H4: The firm-wide increase in the associate billable-hours target is driving the group's associates to resign.
44	H5: The group's resignations reflect ordinary market-wide associate mobility rather than anything specific to the group.
45	R1: Supervision by the partner who joined in October 2025 -> Associate resignation (causes)
46	R2: Assignment to the review workload of the large investigation matter -> Associate resignation (causes)
47	R3: Pay below competing firms -> Associate resignation (causes)
48	R4: Firm-wide billable-target increase -> Elevated resignations in the group (causes)
49	A1: Commission confidential interviews with departed and current Kestrel associates, run by an interviewer outside the group's reporting lines and structured to separate experiences of supervision from experiences of workload, before choosing an intervention.
50	A2: Pay a group-wide retention payment matching the rival firm's quoted pay and close the attrition review as resolved.
51	A3: Move day-to-day supervision of Kestrel associates from the partner who joined in October 2025 to another partner for the rest of the matter.
52	A4: Bring in a firm-funded contract review team to take over first-level document review on Kestrel for the rest of the review phase.
53	A5: Add matter and supervising-partner fields to the firm's attrition reporting and track them monthly from now on.
54	SCORED ITEMS

57	I3: hypothesis H3 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

59	I5: hypothesis H5 allowed=[supported, contradicted, unknown]

61	I7: edge R2 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
62	I8: edge R3 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]
63	I9: edge R4 allowed=[causal, association-only, contradicted, unknown]

65	I11: action A2 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
66	I12: action A3 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]
67	I13: action A4 allowed=[preferred, acceptable, premature, harmful]

Resignations cluster under Faulk (C1: 8 of 11 vs 1 of 13) and E4/C6 contain complaints about him, but Faulk supervises every Kestrel associate and no other matter (C1), so supervision cannot be separated from Kestrel workload (C4, C14); C6 says the reasons were mixed.
